openings.name: Italian — Active (c3/d4, Ng5)
openings.note: Against 3…Bc5: c3 and d4 for a big center; push e5 whenever it kicks the f6 knight. Against 3…Nf6: 4.Ng5 at f7. Every move: is f7 guarded only by the king? Look at Ng5, Qh5/Qf3, Bxf7+.

lines.name: Blackburne Shilling 3…Nd4
lines.note: Do NOT take e5: 4.Nxe5? Qg5! and 5.Nxf7?? Qxg2 6.Rf1 Qxe4+ 7.Be2 Nf3# is mate. Trade on d4 and castle; Re1 and c3 come next.

lines.name: 3…Bc5 — passive 4…d6
lines.note: A big center for free. Don’t rush e5 here (…dxe5 trades queens): tuck the bishop on b3, then Be3, O-O, h3.

lines.name: 3…Bc5 — c3/d4 main
lines.note: Two pawns in the middle. Qb3 hits d5 and f7 together.

lines.name: 3…Bc5 — 7…Nxe4 grab
lines.note: Bxf7+ drags the king out; Qb3+ forks the king and the b4 knight, and f3 traps the e4 knight.

lines.name: Two Knights 4.Ng5 — correct 5…Na5
lines.note: You are a pawn up. Bb5+, Be2, and just develop.

lines.name: TRAP · 5…Nxd5? 6.d4
lines.note: The safer punishment: open lines first, then Nxf7, Qf3+ and Re1+ with the king stuck in the center.

lines.name: TRAP · 5…Nxd5? Fried Liver
lines.note: The pinned d5 knight is the target. Bb3 keeps the pin, a3 kicks the b4 knight, Qe4 piles on, and Nxd5 wins material back with the king exposed.

lines.name: TRAP · Traxler 4…Bc5
lines.note: Not 5.Nxf7? Bxf2+ (chaos). Take with the bishop: the king loses castling and you are simply better.

lines.name: Passive 3…h6 — open the center
lines.note: Black wasted a move: d4 now, while you are ahead in development.

lines.name: TRAP · Legal’s, declined
lines.note: If Black does not take the queen, you have just won a pawn.

lines.name: TRAP · Legal’s Mate
lines.note: Pin on f3 with …Nf6 not played: Nxe5! gives up the queen for mate.

openings.name: Italian — Evans Gambit
openings.note: 3…Bc5 4.b4!? Bxb4 5.c3 and d4. A pawn for time and a huge center; aim at f7 with Qb3 and at the king with Ba3.

lines.name: TRAP · greedy 7…dxc3
lines.note: Three pawns down, but Qb3 hits f7, e5 kicks the queen, and Ba3 pins the king in the center.

lines.name: Accepted, 5…Ba5 — main
lines.note: Ba3 stops Black castling short. Keep the king in the middle.

lines.name: Accepted, 5…Bc5 — normal
lines.note: The classic Evans center: d4 and e4, everything aimed at the Black king.

lines.name: TRAP · 7…Nf6? 8.cxd4 and e5
lines.note: Take back on d4 FIRST so the bishop has to retreat, then e5 kicks the knight to the rim. Bg5 hits the queen; Black is badly behind.

lines.name: Accepted, 5…Be7
lines.note: Black grabs the bishop pair; you get the pawn back and a lead in development.

lines.name: Declined 4…Bb6
lines.note: Gain space on the queenside with a4, then put a knight on d5.

openings.name: Italian — Quiet (Giuoco Pianissimo)
openings.note: Slow build: c3, d3, O-O, Re1, h3, then the knight tour Nbd2–f1–g3. No early fireworks; aim for a later d4 or a kingside push.

lines.name: vs 3…Bc5 — main setup
lines.note: h3 stops …Bg4/…Ng4; Nbd2–f1–g3 reroutes the knight toward f5 and h5.

lines.name: vs 3…Nf6 — Two Knights, quiet
lines.note: Against …Na5, retreat the bishop to c2 via b5–a4 and keep the plan.

openings.name: Scotch (White)
openings.note: Strike the center on move 3 and play with pieces. Watch for: …Qf6 + …Bc5 means check f2 (…Qxf2#); after Nxc6 bxc6, e5 kicks the f6 knight; when …Bb4 pins Nc3, guard e4 first (Bd3/Qd3); look for Nd5 and forks on c7.

lines.name: 3…Nxd4?
lines.note: A dominant queen in the center and a free hand.

lines.name: 3…d6 — Philidor
lines.note: Black is cramped. Pin with Bb5 and develop.

lines.name: 4…Nxd4
lines.note: Same idea: centralized queen. If …Qf6, play e5.

lines.name: 4…Qh4 — Steinitz
lines.note: Looks scary. Just develop: if the queen grabs e4, Nb5 hits c7 and you are far ahead in development.

lines.name: 4…Bc5 — 5.Be3 Qf6 6.c3
lines.note: c3 holds the d4 knight, so the f2 threat goes away.

lines.name: 4…Bc5 — 5.Nxc6 Qf6 6.Qd2
lines.note: After 5.Nxc6, Black threatens …Qxf2#. 6.Qd2 is forced and good; then Nc3 and develop.

lines.name: 4…g6
lines.note: Nxc6 then e5 drives the knight back to g8. Bd4 trades off Black’s best piece.

lines.name: 4…Nf6 — Scotch Four Knights
lines.note: …Bb4 pins Nc3, so e4 is loose: Bd3 guards it. Castle, Bg5, Qf3.

openings.name: 1…d5 — …c5 and …Nc6 vs London
openings.note: Keep 1…d5. Against the London, hit d4 early with …c5 and …Nc6 instead of mirroring.

lines.name: London — …e6 / …Bd6
lines.note: Offer the bishop trade on d6; …b6 and …Bb7 or …Ba6 next.

lines.name: London — …Qb6 hits b2
lines.note: If White skips Nd2/Qb3, …Qb6 wins b2. After the trade, the a-file and …b5–b4 are yours.

lines.name: DEFENSE · London Qb3 vs …Bf5
lines.note: With …Bf5 out, Qb3 hits b7. Let it go: …Nb4 threatens …Nc2+ (the fork you lost to) and …Rb8.

lines.name: DEFENSE · Elephant Trap (QGD)
lines.note: The d4 cousin of Legal’s: the f6 knight looks pinned, but it is not. Nxd5? Nxd5! Bxd8 Bb4+ and you come out a piece up.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit — QGD
lines.note: If White plays 2.c4 instead, the solid Queen’s Gambit Declined.

lines.name: London via 2.Nf3
lines.note: Same plan when White delays Bf4: …c5, …Nc6, …Qb6.

openings.name: 1…e5 — knight before bishop
openings.note: One rule: …Nf6 before …Bc5. The f6 knight blocks the f-file against Qf3 ideas and hits a queen on h5.

lines.name: DEFENSE · Scholar’s Mate 2.Qh5
lines.note: …g6 blocks Qxf7, and when the queen goes to f3, …Nf6 blocks the f-file. Never …Nf6 while the queen is on h5 with e5 loose.

lines.name: DEFENSE · Scholar’s Mate via Bc4/Qf3
lines.note: …Nf6 is the answer to any queen on f3: it covers f7 down the f-file.

lines.name: Scotch Gambit 4.Bc4 — 5.O-O
lines.note: Grab e4, return with …d5; the queen steps to a5 out of the pin.

lines.name: Scotch Gambit 4.Bc4 — 5.e5
lines.note: 4…Nf6 transposes to Two Knights. Strike back with …d5.

lines.name: Scotch 4.Nxd4 — Four Knights
lines.note: Bishop pins the c3 knight once f6 is covered.

lines.name: Scotch 4.Nxd4 — Mieses
lines.note: 6…Qe7 pins the e5 pawn; 8…Ba6 hits c4 against the queen.

lines.name: DEFENSE · 4.Nc3 fork trick
lines.note: If White plays 4.Nc3, take e4: …d5 forks bishop and knight and wins the piece back.

lines.name: Italian 3.Bc4 → Two Knights, 4.d3
lines.note: Knight first, then the bishop comes to c5 safely.

lines.name: DEFENSE · Legal’s-style Nxe5 vs …Bg4
lines.note: Pin with …Bg4 only once …Nf6 is in. If White sacs Nxe5, take it with the pawn: …Bxd1 is still threatened, and with …Nf6 there is no mate. You come out a piece up.

lines.name: Two Knights, 4.Ng5
lines.note: Never recapture 5…Nxd5 (Fried Liver). …Na5 hits the bishop; a pawn down for fast development.

lines.name: DEFENSE · 4.Ng5 … 8.Qf3
lines.note: Qf3 pins c6 to the rook. …Rb8 hits the b5 bishop and frees the pawn.

lines.name: DEFENSE · 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.d3
lines.note: Anti-Fried-Liver: never 5…Nxd5. After 6.d3, kick the knight with …h6 and …e4, grab the bishop.
